scope_note: Post-fifth-pass last-resort modeling gate for Equinix Seattle SE3 retains eight bounded syntheses. Construction is represented separately by the AGC/DJC $50 million-$100 million award-category sensitivity and a 50,482-hours wage benchmark; neither is audited spend or certified payroll. Opening evidence for 24-hour operations and security supports only a conditional one-active-post coverage floor and wage-cost benchmark, not observed posts, headcount, payroll or total staffing. The 2011 lease's up-to-9-MW allocation remains a 25/50/100-percent throughput sensitivity, with separate statewide/tariff price and eGRID NWPP location-based emissions benchmarks that are not bills, measured emissions or market-based results. A medium-confidence identity sets the 2026 same-account assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even threshold equal to the exact landlord-parcel bill; it does not estimate actual public cost, tenant pass-through, cash receipt, recipient distribution or net fiscal impact. A supplier/non-labor residual is rejected because the award category does not define cost coverage and the reported hours do not establish complete labor coverage; community and causal county-effect candidates still fail for lack of compatible inputs or identification.

estimates.label: SE3 lease-capacity annual electricity-throughput sensitivity

period.label: Annualized engineering sensitivity from the executed lease's prospective 9 MW allocation

scope.label: Equinix SE3 leased premises at 2020 Fifth Avenue; no customer, cabinet or meter allocation

interval.interpretation: The lease's up-to-9-MW allocation is annualized at 25%, 50% and 100% utilization. The high endpoint is the mathematical continuous-load ceiling for that contractual allocation, not a forecast, true-value bound or confidence interval.

parameters.name: lease_power_allocation

provenance.detail: Executed lease allocation from two Seattle City Light vaults, limited to 4.5 MW actual draw from either vault

parameters.transformation: Converted to kW and multiplied by annual hours and utilization

provenance.detail: Non-leap-year annualization
Low order-of-magnitude throughput scenario
Central order-of-magnitude throughput scenario
Continuous full-allocation mathematical ceiling

estimates.confidence_rationale: The lease allocation is project specific, but it was prospective, and no public record verifies commissioning, current availability, meter boundary or utilization. The 9 MW may describe utility allocation rather than IT load.
estimates.decision_relevance: Provides an explicit order-of-magnitude throughput sensitivity and contractual ceiling without relabeling allocated capacity as consumption. Separate models apply external price and grid-emissions factors without changing this model into a bill or emissions observation.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Commissioning record, current utility entitlement, interval meter data, bills, peak demand, occupied IT load, site PUE, customer allocation, electricity price, renewable share and emissions

assumptions: The up-to-9-MW lease allocation is used once; the two 4.5 MW vault limits are not added again.
Utilization scenarios are 25%, 50% and 100% solely for sensitivity.
No PUE multiplier is applied because the lease describes tenant electrical allocation and publishes no IT/facility boundary.
The result remains at the SE3 leasehold level and is not allocated by colocation square footage, cabinet count, customer occupancy or assessor area.

limitations: No meter reading, utility bill, observed load factor or commissioning record.
The 2011 prospective allocation may not equal current available, critical IT or occupied load.
The interval is a scenario range, not a statistical or empirical physical bound below the stated ceiling.
This model alone does not infer electricity cost, emissions, revenue, output or fiscal effect.
estimates.notes: Resource sensitivity only. The direct up-to-9-MW source projection remains authoritative; this model is neither observed consumption nor an economic contribution and must not be added to monetary records.

estimates.label: 2026 same-account assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even threshold

period.label: King County tax year 2026 assessed-liability threshold

scope.label: 2020 Fifth Holdings LLC real-property account 065900090500 across the same local taxing jurisdictions; wider than the Equinix leasehold

interval.interpretation: The threshold equals the directly observed same-account 2026 real-property bill by definition; it is not an estimate of actual public cost, cash collected or recipient revenue.

parameters.name: same_account_property_tax_bill

provenance.detail: Sum of all four 2026 billed components for King County real-property account 065900090500

parameters.transformation: Used unchanged as the equal-cost threshold for the same account and tax year

estimates.confidence_rationale: The threshold identity and billed amount are exact, while only partial payments are observed and allocation among taxing jurisdictions and actual marginal public-service cost remain unknown.
estimates.decision_relevance: States the annual public-cost level that would equal the assessed landlord-parcel liability without fabricating a service cost or claiming a positive or negative fiscal margin.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Marginal fire, police, road, utility, administrative, infrastructure and financing costs assigned to the same property account, recipients and tax year; final cash collections and jurisdictional distributions

derivation.formula: same-account assessed-liability public-service cost at break-even = 2026 real-property bill = $391,063.45
assumptions: The threshold is an identity, not an observed or estimated public cost.
The hypothetical cost threshold uses the same landlord property account and tax-year scope as the assessed liability.
The lease's tenant-reimbursement formula is not used to allocate the bill because the annual reconciliation, current garage-space count and replacement comparable-garage rate are unavailable.
The partial payment is not annualized, and unobserved future installments are not treated as paid.
Tenant personal-property tax, incentives, LID incidence, permit values, community gifts and wider portfolio amounts are not netted because their scope, incidence or period does not align.

limitations: This is not an estimate of actual public cost.
The input is the landlord's assessed real-property bill, not an observed Equinix pass-through, tenant payment or proof of full-year collection.
Although the lease provides a reimbursement formula, the current garage deduction and annual reconciliation are unavailable.
The account spans several recipients whose marginal costs and cash timing may differ.
No personal-property account, incentive incidence, marginal service demand or infrastructure cost is included.
No positive or negative net fiscal result is asserted.
estimates.notes: Conditional assessed-liability threshold only. Equality marks break-even against the bill; actual costs, the lease-formula tenant amount and final collections are unknown, so the estimate must not be summed with the tax claim or presented as a fiscal surplus.

estimates.label: SE3 reported-hours construction labor-income benchmark

period.label: Permit issue through final recorded inspection completion; the source does not provide worker-hour dates

scope.label: 2020 Fifth Avenue data-center project labor benchmark; worker residence and employer geography unallocated

interval.interpretation: The 50,482 reported total project worker hours are multiplied by 75%, 100% and 125% of the May 2013 Seattle-Bellevue-Everett construction/extraction mean hourly wage. The range tests unobserved project occupation and wage mix; it is not a confidence interval or a bound on certified payroll or total compensation.

parameters.name: reported_total_project_worker_hours

provenance.detail: AGC/DJC project profile total worker hours

parameters.transformation: Multiplied by the wage benchmark and wage-mix factor

provenance.detail: BLS May 2013 Seattle-Bellevue-Everett major occupational-group mean
Low sensitivity for an SE3 trade and seniority mix below the metropolitan major-group mean
Uses the metropolitan major-group mean without adjustment
High sensitivity for a skilled-trade and overtime mix above the metropolitan major-group mean

estimates.confidence_rationale: The worker-hour total is project specific and the wage is contemporaneous and regional, but the AGC profile is not certified payroll and gives no hours by occupation, straight-time/overtime status, benefits, contractor, date or worker residence. The BLS mean covers King and Snohomish Counties and a broad occupational group.
estimates.decision_relevance: Provides an explicit order-of-magnitude direct construction earnings benchmark from the only project labor quantity found, without deriving worker counts, local-resident income, supplier effects or an input-output multiplier.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Certified payroll, worker-level hours, occupation mix, overtime and fringe benefits, contractor payments, worker residence, calendar distribution and complete project cost

derivation.formula: 50,482 reported worker hours × $27.38 Seattle construction/extraction mean hourly wage × 0.75/1.00/1.25 wage-mix factor
assumptions: The AGC/DJC total worker hours cover the 2020 Fifth Avenue data-center project once and are not duplicated across permits.
The May 2013 metropolitan construction/extraction mean is used as a contemporaneous central earnings benchmark, not asserted as the actual project wage.
The 0.75/1.00/1.25 factors test wage and occupation mix only.
No benefits, payroll taxes, per diem, overtime premium, contractor markup or multiplier is added.
No share is attributed to King County residents or county establishments.

limitations: Not certified payroll or observed worker earnings.
The project-hour source does not disclose its counting method or calendar distribution.
The BLS wage covers a broad two-county occupation group and excludes self-employed workers.
The sensitivity does not estimate worker headcount, job-years, benefits, supplier income, induced effects or local-retained labor income.
The interval is assumption-driven, not statistical.
estimates.notes: Construction earnings benchmark only. It must not be added to permit values, investor funding, rent obligations or accounting basis, and it must not be presented as actual payroll, total compensation, local labor income or permanent employment.

Upper boundary of the published private-building award category

assumptions: The published category applies to the named 2020 Fifth Avenue Data Center project.

estimates.label: Conditional one-post 24x7 SE3 security coverage floor

scope.label: One hypothetical continuously active security post at Equinix SE3; not all security or operations staff

interval.interpretation: One active post for 8,760 hours divided by 2,080 paid hours per FTE-equivalent, with 1.00, 1.15 and 1.30 relief factors. This is a conditional coverage requirement, not observed headcount, jobs or simultaneous-post count.

provenance.detail: One active post continuously covered in a non-leap year

parameters.name: paid_hours_per_fte_equivalent

provenance.detail: 40 hours per week for 52 weeks; a denominator convention, not productive hours observed at SE3

parameters.transformation: Converts annual coverage hours to FTE-equivalents

provenance.detail: No-relief mathematical floor
Illustrative 15% allowance for leave, training and schedule coverage
Illustrative 30% allowance for leave, training and schedule coverage

estimates.confidence_rationale: Equinix explicitly reported 24-hour operations and security at opening and currently reports on-site security, but neither source states that one human post is continuously staffed or identifies employees versus contractors. The relief factors are assumptions.
estimates.decision_relevance: Translates the minimum labor coverage implied only if decision-makers assume one continuously active security post, while preventing 24-hour service language from becoming an unsupported site-employment count.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Whether any post is continuously staffed; simultaneous post count; shift schedules; productive hours; employee/contractor split; total operations and security headcount

derivation.formula: 8,760 annual coverage hours / 2,080 paid hours per FTE-equivalent × 1.00/1.15/1.30 relief factor
assumptions: Exactly one active security post is continuously covered; this is a scenario, not a source claim.
The 24-hour operations and security language remains applicable to the current operating facility.
A 2,080-hour FTE denominator and 1.00/1.15/1.30 relief factors are planning conventions.
No additional post, supervisor, technician, manager, cleaner or contractor is inferred.

limitations: Not observed headcount, employment, jobs, job-years or payroll.
The sources do not establish a continuously staffed post or distinguish human monitoring from systems and remote coverage.
Relief factors are illustrative and do not encode SE3 leave, overtime or scheduling practice.
Does not estimate total facility staffing or King County resident employment.
estimates.notes: Strictly conditional one-post coverage floor. It should be shown only with the antecedent assumption and must not be added to reported employment because no site employment observation exists.

interval.interpretation: The same 19.71/39.42/78.84-GWh throughput endpoints are multiplied by EPA's 635.267 lb CO2e/MWh NWPP total-output rate and converted to metric tons. The interval reflects consumption scenarios only, not uncertainty in the emissions factor.

provenance.detail: Low endpoint of the separately retained lease-capacity throughput sensitivity
Central endpoint of the separately retained lease-capacity throughput sensitivity
Nameplate ceiling of the separately retained lease-capacity throughput sensitivity

parameters.name: nwpp_total_output_emission_rate

provenance.detail: EPA eGRID2023 Revision 2 NWPP total-output rate

parameters.transformation: Converted from pounds to metric tons using 2,204.62262185 lb per metric ton

estimates.confidence_rationale: EPA's factor is authoritative for a regional location-based benchmark, but the consumption is modeled, SE3's meter boundary and supplier mix are unknown, and the factor is neither utility-specific nor contemporaneous with every throughput scenario.
estimates.decision_relevance: Provides a reproducible gross location-based emissions scale for environmental screening without treating capacity as metered use or carbon-neutral/REC claims as measured site emissions reductions.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Metered SE3 electricity, supplier-specific and hourly generation attributes, line loss, contractual instruments, residual mix, market-based Scope 2 accounting and measured backup-generator emissions

derivation.formula: modeled MWh endpoint × 635.267 lb CO2e/MWh / 2,204.62262185 lb per metric ton
assumptions: The retained throughput endpoints are used unchanged.
NWPP is the appropriate broad eGRID subregion for Seattle City Light service.
The eGRID total-output factor is applied without a separate line-loss adjustment.
No REC, power-purchase agreement, utility carbon-neutral claim, avoided-emissions credit or market-based instrument is netted.

limitations: Not measured site emissions or a reported Scope 2 inventory.
The factor is regional and generation-average, not supplier-specific, hourly or marginal.
No market-based adjustment, avoided emissions or backup-generator emissions are included.
The interval is driven by modeled throughput and is not a confidence interval.
estimates.notes: Gross location-based sensitivity only. It must remain distinct from Equinix renewable-energy claims, Seattle City Light's carbon-neutral program and any market-based Scope 2 result.
